items.title: Demat account additions hit 7-month high in August as IPO boom draws investors
items.description: August witnessed a surge in new demat accounts, reaching a seven-month peak due to strong initial public offering activity that spurred many newcomers to the markets. Collectively, NSDL and CDSL welcomed around 3.27 million new accounts, even as benchmark stock indices faced a minor dip. Analysts are optimistic about continued growth, especially with major upcoming IPOs from Jio and NSE on the horizon.

items.title: Stocks in news: Tata Motors, RVNL, Eicher Motors, Mazagon Dock and Lupin
items.description: Indian equity markets experienced volatility, with the Nifty 50 extending its losing streak for four weeks. Escalating US-Iran hostilities pushed crude oil prices higher, impacting overall market sentiment. Several companies, including Tata Motors and Rail Vikas Nigam, are expected to be active on Monday. Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders and Eicher Motors also reported significant corporate developments. Lupin received US FDA approval, while JSW Steel saw production increases in August.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: The Indian equity market ended the week on a positive note, with the Nifty increasing by 0.1 percent on Friday. Factors such as global market trends and easing fears of US interest rate hikes lent support to this rise. The India VIX, often seen as a fear gauge, declined by 5.8 percent, signaling lower market worries.

items.title: AIFs seek status quo as 'foreign control' rules go for a recast
items.description: Local alternative investment funds have warned regulators about proposed changes.  These changes could significantly impact capital inflows into India's economy.  The draft rules aim to curb indirect foreign ownership in sensitive sectors.  Industry officials requested the status quo on existing regulatory definitions.  This move seeks to maintain India's attractiveness for foreign investment.

items.title: RBI's liquidity test may set future course
items.description: The Reserve Bank of India is currently grappling with a notable liquidity dilemma due to a surge in FCNR(B) scheme inflows. To navigate this, a pivotal variable rate reverse repo auction is set to influence the liquidity management strategy. The central bank may also utilize measures such as dollar swaps and bond sales.

items.title: Axis Direct initiates coverage on Pricol with Buy rating. Check target price
items.description: Pricol shares gained after Axis Direct initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a Rs 935 target price, implying around 21% upside. The brokerage expects strong growth through FY29, driven by rising demand for digital instrument clusters, plastics expansion, EV content and global auto orders, while the proposed demerger could unlock additional shareholder value.

items.title: BSE shares surge 10% in just 3 sessions. What’s driving the rally?
items.description: BSE shares extended their winning streak as Sebi announced a review of the methodology used to determine derivative settlement prices following concerns over the new Closing Auction Session. Trading volumes and option activity have declined sharply, particularly at BSE. A consultation paper expected next week could propose changes aimed at reducing expiry-day volatility and improving risk management.

items.title: Nuvoco Vistas among 4 stocks showing White Marubozu pattern
items.description: On September 4, four stocks in the Nifty500 appeared on StockEdge’s ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to its technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest point of the session and the closing price is the highest.The pattern is represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and little to no lower shadow. It reflects strong upward price movement during the session, with the price moving from the opening level to the session high by the close. The pattern is commonly studied in technical analysis as an indicator of strong price momentum.

items.title: Nomura raises target price of stock that’s up over 150% in 2025; stock soars another 6%
items.description: Shares of Avalon Technologies rose sharply on Monday after Nomura raised its target price to Rs 2,767 from Rs 2,211 while retaining a Buy rating. The brokerage said Avalon’s joint venture with Zollner Electronic will expand its capabilities, add global customers and support entry into healthcare, test and measurement, and European markets.

items.title: HFCL shares jump 5% as FY26 order book surges 113% to Rs 21,206 crore
items.description: HFCL shares gained nearly 5% after the company’s FY26 Annual Report highlighted a 113% year-on-year surge in its order book to Rs 21,206 crore. Strong growth in revenue, EBITDA and profit, along with a fresh Rs 2,329 crore export order, further strengthened the company’s growth outlook.

items.title: VA Tech Wabag shares jump 3% after securing repeat order from RIL for ETP project
items.description: VA Tech Wabag shares rose nearly 3% after securing a medium-sized repeat order from Reliance Industries to design and commission an advanced Effluent Treatment Plant at Jamnagar’s Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex. The project will use advanced chemical, biological and sludge treatment technologies and is scheduled for completion within 13 months.

items.title: GST reforms rewrote the auto stock map: Who won, who lost and where can investors still make money?
items.description: The recent GST reforms have significantly impacted the automotive stock market following a rate cut announcement. Notably, Sona BLW Precision Forgings and Samvardhana Motherson International registered impressive growth. Meanwhile, Bajaj Auto, TVS Motor, and Ashok Leyland saw positive movement ahead of their earnings reports. On the downside, stocks like Mahindra & Mahindra and Maruti Suzuki India lagged. Future prospects appear promising, driven by advancements in electric vehicles and fleet modernization.

items.title: PVR Inox shares crash 8% after alleged Rs 200 crore kickback investigation; senior exec's exit comes to light
items.description: PVR Inox shares fell after reports that the company asked senior executive Pramod Arora and others to leave in April following an internal probe into alleged kickbacks of up to ₹200 crore from cinema property developers. The investigation reportedly found irregularities and sought to determine the extent of the alleged wrongdoing.

items.title: ESDS Software extends post-IPO rally, hits 20% upper circuit. Choice Equities sees more upside
items.description: ESDS Software Solution shares extended their post-listing rally, hitting the upper circuit after a strong IPO debut. The stock has surged sharply above its Rs 429 issue price, while Choice Institutional Equities has initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a Rs 1,550 target, citing strong AI infrastructure and cloud growth prospects.

items.title: Buying the smallcap rally? Bear market’s biggest losers crash further in 2026 after falling up to 80%
items.description: In 2026, the performance of smallcap stocks presents a contrasting picture, with half of the top 25 performers bouncing back from significant losses last year. Kabra Extrusiontechnik stands out with a remarkable 150% increase following a previous 59% drop. Conversely, Parsvnath Developers has suffered an additional 85% decline, emphasizing how essential fundamentals are over mere price fluctuations.

items.title: Exclusive | How Vijay Kedia turned a Rs 250 Neuland Labs bet into nearly 100x returns
items.description: Investor Vijay Kedia's savvy investment in Neuland Laboratories has paid off handsomely, yielding nearly 100x returns. He seized the opportunity during the Covid downturn when stock prices dipped. By concentrating on the company’s promising peptide sector and its CDMO capabilities, Kedia emphasized his tactic of investing in overlooked firms with solid fundamentals, which has ultimately fostered substantial wealth growth over the years.

items.title: Sensex drops over 250 points, Nifty falls below 23,850. Why is market falling despite positive fundamental factors?
items.description: Indian stock markets experienced a decline on Monday as rising oil costs and geopolitical unrest took their toll. The technology sector saw the steepest losses, while overall market activity reflected a varied response. Analysts cite ongoing risks from Middle East conflicts, alongside a robust pipeline of upcoming IPOs expected to influence market liquidity significantly this September. Moreover, concerns over potential US interest rate increases are further complicating the economic landscape.

items.title: Top Nifty50 stocks analysts suggest buying in this volatile week
items.description: Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, is a comprehensive report that evaluates five key components of 4,000+ listed stocks – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum – to generate standardised scores. The simple average of the above-mentioned five component ratings is normally distributed to reach an average score.

items.title: ICICI Bank shares in focus as LIC gets RBI nod to acquire 9.99% stake in private lender
items.description: ICICI Bank shares will be in focus after RBI approved LIC to acquire up to 9.99% in the lender within one year. LIC already holds over 4%. Despite recent weakness, ICICI Bank has gained 6% in 2026, with strong long-term returns. Major brokerages remain bullish on the stock.

items.title: Hindustan Unilever shares in focus as Capital Markets Day outlines growth levers; what are Goldman Sachs and Nomura saying?
items.description: Hindustan Unilever’s Capital Markets Day outlined a strategy focused on consumption-led growth, premiumisation, market-making and new growth spaces. Goldman Sachs, Nuvama and Nomura retained Buy ratings, with target prices ranging from Rs 2,450 to Rs 2,820. HUL has raised medium-term margin guidance to 22-24%, while higher capex and underpenetrated categories are expected to support growth.

items.title: Tata Motors shares in focus as firm launches tender offer for Iveco Group; values company at €3.82 billion
items.description: Tata Motors has launched a voluntary tender offer to acquire all common shares of Iveco Group for €14.1 per share in cash, valuing the Italian commercial vehicle maker at about €3.82 billion. Backed by Iveco’s largest shareholder, Exor, the deal aims to take Tata Motors’ commercial vehicle business global and could lead to Iveco’s delisting from Euronext Milan.

items.title: FIIs raise stakes in 9 midcap stocks for four straight quarters; shares surge up to 70% in a year
items.description: Tracking Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) can offer useful insights, as their investment decisions are typically backed by extensive research and analysis. Over the four quarters through June 2026, FIIs steadily increased their holdings in around 15 BSE midcap stocks. Of these, 9 gained 10%-70% over the past year. (Data source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Muthoot FinCorp rolls out Rs 700 crore NCD issue. Here's what investors need to know
items.description: Muthoot FinCorp has launched the fifth tranche of its secured, rated and redeemable NCDs, offering effective annual yields of 8.89% to 9.25% across four tenures ranging from 24 to 72 months. The company aims to raise up to Rs 700 crore, with proceeds earmarked for onward lending, repayment or prepayment of existing borrowings and general corporate purposes.

items.title: Why Systematix is bullish on Apollo Micro Systems after 47% YTD rally; check target price
items.description: Systematix initiated coverage of Apollo Micro Systems with a Buy rating and Rs 570 target, citing defence-system integration, a Rs 12,000-crore opportunity, capacity expansion, acquisitions and strong earnings growth, while flagging execution, working-capital and tender-related risks.

items.title: Stock picks of the week: 5 stocks with consistent score improvement and upside potential of up to 23%
items.description: As oil prices move up again, how will things pan out for the Indian market? Will it be a standalone underperformer? Or is it just a phase where the rising price of crude is leading to fears that the market will again come under pressure in the short term? Our selected stocks for today depict a strong upward trajectory in their overall average score which is based on five key pillars: Earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum. This implies that there has been a significant improvement in their market outlook in the given time frame.

items.title: SRK, Madhuri Dixit-backed Purple Style Labs makes weak D-Street debut. Should you buy?
items.description: Purple Style Labs commenced trading on Monday at a discount, despite its initial public offering being fully subscribed. The acquisition of Pernia's Pop-Up Shop in 2018 played a role in the considerable revenue growth from FY20 to FY24. Nevertheless, analysts caution investors regarding the expanding losses and the company's currently high valuation.

items.title: India’s Rs 1 lakh crore digital-media boom: Two stocks ICICI Securities is betting on
items.description: India’s digital media market crossed Rs 1 lakh crore in CY25 and is projected to grow rapidly through CY28, while television revenue declines. ICICI Securities has initiated coverage on Amagi Media Labs and Prime Focus with Buy ratings, citing opportunities from cloud adoption, digital advertising, VFX spending and evolving content consumption.

items.title: India in multi quarter growth upcycle, says Morgan Stanley; sees Sensex at 89,000 by June 2027
items.description: Morgan Stanley sees India entering a multi-quarter growth upcycle, supported by improving investments, monetary policy and domestic demand. The brokerage expects the Sensex to reach 89,000 by June 2027 in its base case, while assigning 25% probabilities to a bull-case target of 100,000 and a bear-case target of 66,000.

items.title: Motilal Oswal sees 27% upside in this retail stock; should you buy?
items.description: Motilal Oswal initiated coverage on V2 Retail with a Buy rating and a ₹275 target, implying around 27% upside. The brokerage is bullish on the retailer’s tier-II/III focus, strong store economics, high private-label mix and disciplined inventory management, which it believes offer significant room for growth.

items.title: Sebi’s new ETF rules apply today: What changes from September 7 and how they impact investors?
items.description: Sebi’s revised ETF trading rules have come into effect from September 7, changing how price bands and reference prices are determined. The new framework introduces dynamic price bands based on underlying assets and a pre-open auction for gold and silver ETFs, aiming to improve price discovery and reduce premiums or discounts to NAV.

items.title: Infosys, HCLTech, TCS, other IT stocks drop up to 3% as Fed rate hike worries return. Here's why
items.description: Indian IT stocks dropped on Monday as stronger-than-expected US jobs data revived concerns over a September Federal Reserve rate hike. The Nifty IT index dropped over 2%, with Infosys, HCLTech, TCS and others declining. Analysts, however, see longer-term opportunities from AI-led spending on deployment, integration and modernisation.

items.title: Did HEG shares really crash 64% in one day? Here’s how the demerger math works
items.description: HEG shares opened nearly 64% lower on Monday as the stock adjusted for the company’s demerger, which split its businesses into two separately listed entities. The graphite electrodes business will move to HEG Graphite, while the existing listed company will retain advanced materials, battery energy solutions and green power businesses and be renamed HEG Advanced Materials.

items.title: IFCI shares rally 6%, turn multibagger as NSE IPO gets SEBI nod. More upside ahead?
items.description: IFCI shares rallied 6% after Sebi approved NSE’s much-awaited IPO, clearing a key hurdle for the exchange’s listing. IFCI has indirect exposure to NSE through its majority stake in Stock Holding Corporation of India. The stock has surged over 500% in three years, with analysts seeing further upside.

items.title: Wires on fire: Why UltraTech’s Rs 1,800 crore Ultravolt bet wiped out Rs 21,500 crore in 2 days
items.description: UltraTech’s entry into wires and cables triggered a sharp selloff in listed peers as investors assess the impact of intensified competition on market share, pricing and margins. While house wires and light-duty cables face the most immediate pressure, higher-voltage segments remain relatively insulated. Analysts remain positive on long-term industry growth, but caution that elevated valuations leave incumbents vulnerable.
